articles.title: Football Daily - Carrick Stays at United & Kane Wins Ballon d’Or - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Carrick stays at United. Kane wins Ballon d’Or, Putellas claims third Women’s award.
articles.body:
Radio 5 Live , · 27 Oct 2026 , · 30 mins

Kelly Somers is joined by Andy Reid, Leon Osman & Ian Dennis to discuss Michael Carrick remaining in charge at Manchester United after eight games without a win, despite links to Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. Man Utd fan Scott Saunders gives the supporters’ reaction, while Raphael Honigstein discusses the Nagelsmann links. Then, reaction to Harry Kane winning the Ballon d’Or - the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001. Former England teammate Conor Coady joins, with more from Honigstein on the reaction in Germany and at Bayern. Finally, London City Lionesses CEO Martin Semmens on Alexia Putellas winning the Ballon d’Or Féminin for a third time after her move to the WSL.

articles.title: Over-the-counter teeth whitening: What products really work and how to make it last
articles.summary: Experts share the best over-the-counter teeth whitening products of 2026 for a brighter smile, including Crest Whitestrips, Sensodyne and whitening pens.
articles.body: A professional whitening treatment at the dentist’s office is the fastest and most effective way to see results, but it’s costly and time consuming. If you’re leaning toward using over-the-counter teeth whitening products, there’s no shortage of options, like strips, gels, toothpastes and mouthwashes. But do they work? It depends on which one you use, how well you follow the directions and what your expectations are. To help you choose an option that addresses your needs, I talked to dentists about the pros and cons of each type of OTC teeth whitening product, including when (and if) you’ll see a visible difference in tooth color. Using experts’ guidance, I rounded up the best options from brands like Crest, Sensodyne, Act and Colgate, many of which the NBC Selected team tested. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best OTC teeth whitening products of 2026 All of the over-the-counter teeth whitening products below meet experts’ guidance (learn more about how experts recommend shopping for them here). I included options with the American Dental Association’s Seal of Acceptance, those NBC Selected staff members have tested, NBC Selected Wellness Award-winners and other highly rated treatments. Best OTC teeth whitening strips and trays No matter how many times our team tests teeth whitening strips, Crest’s come out on top for two reasons: they work and they’re easy to use. The strips are coated in hydrogen peroxide gel and have a non-slip grip, which helps them stay put during treatments — I can have full conversations while wearing them and they don’t budge, plus they’re so thin that I barely feel them. The Whitestrips are flexible, so I can bend them around the curve of my teeth, but they’re sturdy enough that they don’t roll in on themselves when I take them off the packaging. This box comes with enough strips for 20 45-minute treatments and two 1-hour express treatments. Former NBC Selected senior editor Lindsay Schneider finds Opalescence’s whitening trays easier to apply than whitening strips — you bite into them and they mold around the shape of your teeth. “They’re so easy to pop on and off, and I find them comfortable to wear for longer periods of time,” says Schneider. Her dentist recommended these trays, which you leave on for about 30 minutes, because they’re made with a professional-grade, 10% hydrogen peroxide, minty gel. “I definitely see a difference when using these consistently — my teeth are noticeably whiter,” says Schneider. “Because they’re stronger, my teeth get a little sensitive when using them, but that’s the case with almost all whitening products for me.” Opalescence’s whitening gel, which you add to custom trays a dentist makes, is professional-grade like its trays. Its main active ingredient is carbamide peroxide, and there’s also hydrogen peroxide in its formula. The gel is available in four concentrations, 10%, 15%, 20% and 35%, each of which has a different treatment time ranging from 30 minutes to overnight. It comes in syringes with a narrow nozzle, helping you fill your trays without causing them to overflow. The gel is available in mint and melon flavors, as well as an unflavored option. Best OTC teeth whitening toothpaste All of the whitening toothpastes below have fluoride in their formulas to protect teeth from cavities and repair enamel. Every member of our team who tested this toothpaste had the same review: it’s shockingly effective. “My coffee-stained teeth started visibly whitening in just days, so much so that my dentist thought I’d gotten a professional treatment,” says NBC Selected editorial director Lauren Swanson. The minty toothpaste is made with hydrated silica, which dissolves the bonds that adhere stains to teeth and scrubs them off the surface, according to the brand. The toothpaste comes in a pump dispenser, which prevents you from using too much at a time. In addition to teeth whitening trays and gel, Opalescence makes whitening toothpaste, which is a top pick among our staff members. There’s silica in its formula to gently remove surface stains, and after using it for a few weeks, NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi says her teeth are visibly brighter. The toothpaste also doesn’t feel harsh on or irritate her teeth, which wasn’t the case with other options she’s tried. It has a gel texture and a cool mint flavor. Sensodyne makes some of our favorite toothpastes for sensitive teeth, and this option offers additional whitening benefits. Its formula has hydrated silica to buff stains away, plus it’s made with stannous fluoride, which relieves sensitivity while fighting cavities, according to the brand. “I’ve always had really sensitive teeth, especially to cold, and I’m always nervous to do whitening treatments,” says former NBC senior community manager Rosalie Sparaco. “Having a toothpaste that can help my teeth feel less sensitive to cold drinks while whitening is a win-win.” The toothpaste gets very foamy as you brush, and it has a cool peppermint and spearmint flavor. After using this whitening toothpaste, your mouth gets anti-bacterial protection for up to 24 hours, according to the brand. The hydrated silica in its formula fades surface stains and yellowing, and consistent use can also help with issues like plaque and tartar buildup, according to the brand. The toothpaste has a refreshing mint flavor and it doesn’t get very foamy while you’re using it, in my experience. Best OTC whitening mouthwash ACT’s Whitening + Anticavity mouthwash uses hydrogen peroxide to brighten your teeth and fluoride to prevent cavities. It’s free-from alcohol and dyes, according to the brand, and has a mint flavor to freshen breath. Best OTC teeth whitening pen Colgate’s whitening pen is filled with hydrogen peroxide gel, and its overall construction resembles lipstick. You unscrew the attached brush, dip it into the gel and apply it on your teeth. The brush is very small, so you can coat one tooth at a time and make sure you don’t miss a spot. The brand recommends applying the quick-dry gel before bed, leaving it on your teeth overnight and brushing it off in the morning. How to shop for OTC teeth whitening products What are the different types of OTC teeth whitening products? There’s seven main types of over-the-counter teeth whitening products to know about, all of which I explain below. To decide which one is right for you, think about what fits into your lifestyle — these products only work if you use them consistently. Whitening strips: These are essentially stickers for your upper and lower teeth that are coated with a thin layer of an active bleaching ingredient, like hydrogen peroxide. As the strips sit on your teeth, the ingredients penetrate enamel to brighten it. Whitening trays: These work similarly to strips, but you bite into them rather than adhere them to the front of teeth. Most trays come prefilled with whitening gel formulated with active bleaching ingredients — if not, you’ll need to fill them with gel before a treatment.Whitening gel with custom trays: Over-the-counter whitening trays are one size fits all, which not everyone finds comfortable or effective. Instead, your dentist can make you custom trays that fit the exact shape of your mouth, and you can buy whitening gel made with active bleaching ingredients to fill them with. “Using custom whitening trays made by your dentist can isolate where the whitening material goes,” says Dr. Erin Fraundorf, the founder and orthodontist at Boca Orthodontic and Whitening Studio. “You can better control it to prevent it from touching your gum tissue.Whitening toothpaste: Whitening toothpaste mainly relies on abrasives rather than active bleaching ingredients to remove surface stains from teeth, according to the ADA. All toothpaste is mildly abrasive to scrub teeth clean, but whitening toothpaste has abrasives that specifically target surface stains, like sodium bicarbonate (baking soda).Whitening mouthwash: Whitening mouthwash has active bleaching ingredients in its formula that break down stains on your teeth as you swish the liquid around in your mouth.Whitening pens: These help you brighten teeth quickly and while on the go. They’re filled with a gel made from active bleaching ingredients, which you brush on your teeth and leave on for a specified period of time. LED light kits: Some whitening strips and trays come with an LED light, which many brands advertise as being able to enhance or accelerate the whitening process. However, the dentists I talked to don’t recommend using them, so I didn’t add any to the list above. “Not all LED lights are created equal, and the ones included in at-home whitening kits are significantly weaker than those used in professional treatments,” says Fraundorf. “Whether or not you use an LED light with your at-home whitening kit, your results will be the same.” Which OTC teeth whitening products are the most effective? Over-the-counter teeth whitening strips, trays and gels for custom trays are typically the most effective because they’re made with high concentrations of active ingredients, according to the experts I talked to. The more concentrated a product’s active whitening ingredients are, the stronger it is. Whitening toothpaste, mouthwash and pens tend to have low concentrations of active ingredients, so their impact is minimal, says Dr. Matt Messina, an assistant professor at The Ohio State University College of Dentistry. He recommends using them as a maintenance tool after a stronger treatment, and says their ideal for beginners. If you’ve never whitened your teeth before or have a history of tooth sensitivity, start with products that have a low concentration of active ingredients and gradually increase if you can tolerate it. What are the most common active ingredients in OTC teeth whitening products? Hydrogen and carbamide peroxide are the two most common whitening agents in dental care products, over-the-counter or professional, according to the ADA. The active ingredients penetrate tooth enamel and break down discoloration without softening or thinning teeth, experts say. Can OTC teeth whitening products earn the ADA Seal of Acceptance? Yes, over-the-counter teeth whitening products can earn the ADA Seal of Acceptance. The ADA Seal of Acceptance is the gold standard for dental care products. Brands can voluntarily submit data for the ADA to review, and if the organization deems the product safe and effective according to specific criteria, it earns the seal. This doesn’t mean that whitening products without the seal are ineffective — it just means brands haven’t submitted their products for the ADA to review. Meet our oral care experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Matt Messina is an assistant professor at The Ohio State University College of Dentistry and the clinic director of Ohio State’s Upper Arlington Dentistry.Dr. Ilona Casellini is the founder of and a dentist at Swiss Quality Smile.Dr. Erin Fraundorf is the founder and orthodontist at Boca Orthodontic and Whitening Studio. Why trust NBC Selected? I’m a reporter at NBC Selected who has written about dental care for over five years, including stories on electric toothbrushes, toothpaste, whitening toothpaste, kid’s toothpaste, floss and water flossers. For this article, I interviewed three experts about how to shop for over-the-counter teeth whitening treatments and I rounded up options that align with dentists’ guidance, including products the NBC Select staff tested. I also constantly test oral care products to share my first-hand experience using them and stay up-to-date about innovations in the industry. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Justiça revoga prisão preventiva de Gabriel Spalone, preso em Guarulhos por suspeita de extorsão | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão aponta dúvida sobre o caráter indevido da vantagem econômica exigida em disputa comercial envolvendo investimentos em criptoativos; empresário deverá usar tornozeleira eletrônica e cumprir medidas cautelares.
articles.summary: Decisão aponta dúvida sobre o caráter indevido da vantagem econômica exigida em disputa comercial envolvendo investimentos em criptoativos; empresário deverá usar tornozeleira eletrônica e cumprir medidas cautelares.
articles.body:
Gabriel Spalone é empresário e influenciador digital e foi preso novamente em São Paulo. — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

A Justiça revogou a prisão preventiva do empresário e influencer Gabriel Spalone Alves, que está preso no Centro de Detenção Provisória (CDP) de Guarulhos, na Grande São Paulo , alvo de uma operação policial em 2025 contra um esquema suspeito de desviar R$ 146 milhões por meio do PIX .

A decisão é do juiz Fabio Martins Marsiglio, que determinou a adoção de medidas cautelares, entre elas o uso de tornozeleira eletrônica, a proibição de contato com os denunciantes e seus familiares e a restrição de aproximação a menos de 500 metros deles.

Gabriel é acusado de extorsão, crime previsto no artigo 158 do Código Penal. Na decisão, o magistrado considerou que documentos apresentados pela defesa trouxeram novos elementos ao caso e apontaram uma possível controvérsia comercial entre os envolvidos sobre valores relacionados a investimentos em criptoativos.

Procurado, o advogado Eduardo Maurício, que representa Gabriel Spalone, afirmou que o processo tramita em segredo de Justiça, mas confirmou a revogação da prisão preventiva.

Em nota, o advogado classificou a decisão como assertiva e em conformidade com a lei. Segundo ele, a medida seria uma prova da inocência do empresário, que, de acordo com a defesa, nunca praticou crime de extorsão.

O advogado também afirmou que o caso decorre de uma manobra de terceiros que, segundo ele, se apresentaram como vítimas para evitar o pagamento de valores que seriam devidos legalmente ao empresário.

A defesa sustenta que o caso envolve um desacerto comercial entre as empresas Life Coin e CargoBR. Conforme a decisão judicial, Gabriel apresentou um boletim de ocorrência registrado em 11 de junho de 2026, antes da notícia-crime apresentada pelos denunciantes, em 20 de agosto de 2026.

O documento foi considerado pelo magistrado com conversas entre o empresário e o advogado Bruno Bonametti de Miranda, que representa os denunciantes e foi defensor de Gabriel anteriormente, além de relatórios técnicos apresentados ao processo.

A Justiça, porém, não declarou a inocência do empresário nem encerrou a ação penal. A decisão trata da necessidade de manutenção da prisão preventiva e afirma que a discussão sobre a existência do crime será examinada durante a instrução processual.

Spalone teve a prisão preventiva decretada em 9 de outubro e foi encaminhado ao Centro de Detenção Provisória (CDP) de Osasco , na Grande São Paulo.

Ele foi preso sob a suspeita de extorquir e ameaçar dois empresários dizendo que era integrante do Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC). O mandado de prisão temporária de cinco dias foi realizado por policiais civis da 1ª Delegacia Antissequestro, do Departamento de Operações Policiais Estratégicas (Dope).

Para a defesa do influenciador, "a conversão da prisão temporária em preventiva em apenas 2 dias desde a prisão demonstra a ilegalidade e a perseguição que o empresário e influencer vem sofrendo, tanto por parte da polícia e do Ministério Público".

"A defesa irá requerer a revogação da prisão preventiva e, se for o caso, impetrar habeas corpus, pois nunca existiu ameaça, extorsão e vínculo com o PCC, e ficará provada a sua inocência na instrução processual", afirmou o advogado Eduardo Maurício.

Spalone é acusado de ameaçar Marcio Eduardo Nozari e Marcel Rosica Anconi, sócios da empresa Cargobr Transportes Ltda., em meio a uma disputa envolvendo uma dívida milionária.

Segundo a acusação, após ser solto no âmbito da investigação sobre o suposto desvio de R$ 146 milhões, o influenciador passou a cobrar dos empresários uma quantia que alegava ter a receber.

Os empresários, por sua vez, alegam ter compensado a dívida com valores relacionados a outro negócio envolvendo Márcio e Spalone, que teria resultado em prejuízo financeiro.. A divergência sobre essa compensação teria motivado as cobranças.

Ainda de acordo com a denúncia, Spalone passou a ameaçar os dois empresários e o advogado deles, identificado como Bruno. O influenciador teria afirmado ser integrante do Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) e ameaçado sequestrar familiares dos três caso não recebesse o dinheiro exigido.

Diante das denúncias, a Justiça de Osasco autorizou a prisão temporária do influenciador, que passou por audiência de custódia nesta sexta-feira (9). De acordo com o Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo, a audi foi apenas para verificar se houve alguma irregularidade no cumprimento dessa prisão. Não foram identificadas irregularidades e ele segue preso."

Ele responde processo criminal por furto qualificado e associação criminosa , justamente pelo esquema ilegal dos R$ 146 milhões investigados pela polícia de São Paulo.

🔴Difusão Vermelha, também conhecida como "lista vermelha" é um mecanismo internacional para o compartilhamento de informações de foragidos internacionais. Atualmente, a organização possui 19 bancos de dados à disposição das polícias do mundo, entre eles, de impressões digitais, perfis de DNA, documentos falsificados e obras de arte, por exemplo.

De acordo com a Polícia Federal, a prisão foi feita com apoio da Polícia Civil de São Paulo e das autoridades da Argentina, Panamá, Paraguai e Estados Unidos.

Após viajar a Dubai, ele foi detido no Panamá, mas acabou liberado por não estar na lista da Interpol. Horas depois, ele foi incluído no alerta vermelho da organização internacional, o que o fez ser preso em Buenos Aires. Depois disso, ele foi extraditado para o Brasil.

Em 2025, a Delegacia de Crimes Cibernéticos da Polícia Civil de São Paulo fez uma operação para cumprir mandados de busca e apreensão e prisão temporária contra Gabriel Spalone, mas o influenciador não foi encontrado.

Ele é suspeito de participação em um esquema que desviou R$ 146 milhões via PIX de um banco e de empresas vítimas das transferências ilegais. Outras duas pessoas foram presas. Guilherme Sateles Coelho e Jesse Mariano da Silva teriam se beneficiado em quase R$ 75 milhões do esquema.

Os investigadores dizem que o esquema envolvia empresas criadas por Gabriel Spalone, que ofereciam serviços financeiros digitais, como transações de câmbio, criptomoedas e pagamentos.

Elas não tinham autorização do Banco Central para operar transferências diretas via PIX. Então, usavam o sistema de bancos ou empresas financeiras que têm autorização para realizar a operação. Esta intermediação é o chamado o PIX indireto, que é ilegal desde janeiro, quando o Banco Central endureceu regras para fintechs, como as de Gabriel.

Segundo a polícia, em fevereiro deste ano, as empresas dele realizaram em menos de 5 horas mais de 600 transferências ilegais por PIX indireto, de 10 contas de um único banco, totalizando R$ 146 milhões. O banco conseguiu identificar a fraude e recuperar R$ 100 milhões.

Policiais cumprem mandados de busca e apreensão de carros e entram em imóveis de investigados no esquema de fraude com o PIX em São Paulo — Foto: Reprodução/Divulgação

articles.title: Resultado Lotofácil 3815: duas apostas de MT ganham R$ 1,9 mil cada | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogos simples registrados em Comodoro e Juína acertaram 14 dezenas; prêmio principal saiu para três apostas de outros estados.
articles.summary: Jogos simples registrados em Comodoro e Juína acertaram 14 dezenas; prêmio principal saiu para três apostas de outros estados.
articles.body:
Duas apostas feitas em Mato Grosso ficaram a um número de levar o prêmio principal do concurso 3815 da Lotofácil , sorteado nesta terça-feira (27). Cada uma acertou 14 das 15 dezenas e ganhou R$ 1.943,41.

Os jogos premiados foram registrados em Comodoro e Juína . As duas apostas foram simples, com 15 números marcados em cada uma.

Em todo o país, 200 apostas acertaram 14 números e receberam R$ 1.943,41 cada. Já as três apostas que acertaram as 15 dezenas, premiadas com R$ 432.535,38 cada, foram registradas em Salvador (BA), Brusque (SC) e Iporã do Oeste (SC).

articles.title: Brasileira morre durante viagem à Espanha após disputar meia maratona | G1
articles.standfirst: Natural de Porto Alegre, oftalmologista viajava com a mãe e aproveitava férias após participar de prova em Valência.
articles.summary: Natural de Porto Alegre, oftalmologista viajava com a mãe e aproveitava férias após participar de prova em Valência.
articles.body:
Médica e corredora Victoria d'Azevedo Silveira — Foto: Reprodução/ Redes sociais; Arquivo pessoal

Uma viagem que havia começado com esporte e planos de descanso terminou em tragédia para a família da médica oftalmologista Victoria d'Azevedo Silveira , 29 anos. Natural de Porto Alegre , ela morreu durante uma viagem à Espanha . A jovem estava acompanhada da mãe.

Segundo a tia, Zélia Silveira d'Azevedo, a programação inicial da médica incluía a participação de Victoria na Meia Maratona de Valência , no domingo (25). Após completar a corrida, elas saíram para comer, descansaram, e, no fim da tarde, embarcaram em um trem para Barcelona.

Na manhã seguinte, ela não acordou. A causa da morte ainda não foi esclarecida .

O corpo foi encaminhado ao instituto responsável pelos exames periciais. A autópsia foi realizada, mas o laudo ainda não havia sido entregue à família até esta terça-feira (27) , segundo Zélia.

Conforme os familiares, o corpo também aguardava liberação oficial para que os demais procedimentos pudessem ser realizados.

A família informou que já entrou em contato com a seguradora e com o consulado brasileiro na Espanha.

"Essa espera nos angustia", relata a tia Zélia.

Victoria era médica oftalmologista especializada em glaucoma e, segundo a tia, tinha uma trajetória marcada pela dedicação aos estudos e à profissão.

"Era uma luz na nossa família. Não havia quem não gostasse dela", afirma Zélia.

Filha única e muito ligada aos familiares, Victoria também mantinha uma rotina voltada ao esporte . Corredora apaixonada , treinava desde 2020 com a Cia dos Cavalos e participava regularmente de provas.

De acordo com a tia, a médica levava os treinos a sério, mantinha cuidados rigorosos com a alimentação e com a atividade física e estava especialmente feliz com o desempenho obtido na Espanha.

Segundo a família, ela comentou que havia feito sua melhor corrida e terminou a prova como a segunda brasileira mais bem colocada.

"Estava radiante", relembra a tia. "Ela estava feliz, fazendo uma coisa que amava e ao lado da mãe, que amava muito", disse Zélia.

articles.title: Procuradora de Macaé ataca petistas, nordestinos e mineiros em post | G1
articles.standfirst: Renata Pinto Rodrigues Pimentel Ribeiro ainda pediu para mineiros saírem de Macaé, e completou: 'Já basta o Espírito Santo que vocês invadem feito tralha'. Entidades repudiaram a atitude da procuradora.
articles.summary: Renata Pinto Rodrigues Pimentel Ribeiro ainda pediu para mineiros saírem de Macaé, e completou: 'Já basta o Espírito Santo que vocês invadem feito tralha'. Entidades repudiaram.
articles.body:
A procuradora do município de Macaé (RJ), Renata Pinto Rodrigues Pimentel Ribeiro, fez uma postagem nas redes sociais, nesta terça-feira (27), declarando que não fará mais política pública para petistas, referindo-se a eles como "esse tipo de gente", e ainda sugeriu que empresas não contratem "artistas, pobres nordestinos e mineiros".

A Polícia Civil informou que instaurou um inquérito para investigar o caso. As declarações também foram repudiadas pela Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB).

"Petistas não vão trabalhar pra mim, não vou fazer mais política pública pra poder ajudar esse tipo de gente. Aconselho a todos os empresários, microempresários a não contratarem artistas, pobres nordestinos e mineiros", disse em trecho da postagem.

"Aliás, mineiros saem de Macaé! Já basta o Espírito Santo que vocês invadem feito tralha", expressou, afirmando ainda que ganha bem e que "Eu e meus filhos vão ter tudo do bom e do melhor".

Procuradora afirmou, em redes sociais, que não contrataria nem ajudaria pessoas em razão do posicionamento político e chegou a orientar empresários a não contratarem nordestinos e mineiros. — Foto: Redes sociais

Após a repercussão do caso também voltaram a circular publicações antigas atribuídas a ela na rede social X. Em uma delas, publicada em 2025, a procuradora escreveu que, se pudesse, “metralhava” pessoas de esquerda.

"Não tenho palavras para descrever estes nazistas de esquerda! Se eu pudesse metralhava a todos sem distinção! Estamos em guerra mesmo! Morte aos esquerdistas", escreveu no post.

Renata afirmou que não pretende apagar as mensagens. — Foto: Redes sociais

A OAB destacou que a liberdade de expressão não autoriza discriminação, hostilidade ou exclusão de pessoas em razão da origem, da condição social, da orientação sexual ou do posicionamento político.

A repercussão chegou à Câmara Municipal de Macaé . Durante a sessão desta terça-feira, vereadores criticaram as declarações e defenderam a apuração do caso. O presidente da Casa, Luciano Diniz , afirmou que espera o encaminhamento da situação à Procuradoria para as providências cabíveis.

O PT de Macaé também se manifestou. Em nota assinada pelo presidente do partido, professor Paulo Henrique, a sigla afirmou que as declarações ultrapassam o campo da disputa política e atingem a dignidade de pessoas que vivem e trabalham na cidade.

O partido informou ainda que acionou o Ministério Público e a Ouvidoria-Geral do Município, pedindo a apuração do caso e a adoção das medidas cabíveis, caso seja confirmada alguma conduta ilícita, com garantia do direito de defesa.

A Prefeitura de Macaé informou que o caso foi encaminhado à Procuradoria-Geral do Município e que as medidas administrativas cabíveis estão sendo analisadas pelos órgãos competentes. A administração também afirmou que as declarações atribuídas à servidora não representam os valores nem a posição institucional do município.

Ao g1 , Renata afirmou que as publicações estavam em perfis privados e alegou ter sido traída por pessoas próximas, que fizeram capturas de tela e divulgaram o material.

"Eu tava de cabeça quente, realmente, quando eu mandei os nordestinos. Os mineiros, inclusive, meu pai é mineiro, tá? Meu pai falecido, era mineiro, meu avô é mineiro. Tava de cabeça quente, como milhares de pessoas fizeram isso. É uma loucura, tô sendo ameaçada de morte", disse Renata. Pimentel Ribeiro.

Quanto à prestação de serviço público à população e ao conselho para empresas não darem emprego a petistas, Renata comentou:

"Eu, como procuradora, continuaria fazendo minhas políticas públicas como eu sempre fiz, agindo com imparcialidade, com integralidade dos meus atos. Agora, eu falei: 'Não dê emprego'. Pô, quando a gente tá de cabeça quente, a gente fala umas coisas que não fala, né?... Você tá entendendo? A gente bota filho de castigo, a gente faz milhões de coisas.

Ao ser questionada se ela se arrependia da publicação, disse:

"Eu publiquei no meu perfil privado do Facebook. Nem do Instagram foi. No meu perfil privado do Facebook, eu falei de cabeça quente. Até umas pessoas pegaram e falaram assim: 'Tira, tira'. Não tem como tirar, não tiro mais não, porque seria um ato covarde meu.

articles.title: Alexander brothers, ex-luxury real estate brokers, sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking
articles.summary: Federal prosecutors were seeking life sentences for Oren, Alon and Tal Alexander.
articles.body:
Two former luxury real estate brokers and their brother were each sentenced to 30 years in federal prison, seven months after they were convicted of drugging and raping women in a sex trafficking ring.

Federal prosecutors sought life sentences for Oren and Alon Alexander, a pair of former powerful real estate brokers, and their brother, Tal, in a New York City courtroom Tuesday afternoon. Attorneys for the brothers, who have asserted their innocence, asked the judge to give the men the mandatory minimum, instead.

U.S. District Judge Valerie Caproni characterized the brothers as "Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde." On one side, they were described as gentlemen who loved their children, she said, and on the other, they were described as "sadistic, misogynistic, sexual predators."

"Your conduct was monstrous," Caproni said in her sentencing.

But Caproni added that she did not believe the Alexander brothers were beyond redemption, declining the request to give them life sentences.

In addition to 30 years of incarceration, she ordered 10 years of supervised release and sex offender treatment approved by the probation office. They are not to have contact with any child under age 18 unless it is approved by the probation office.

Twins Alon and Oren Alexander, 39, were ordered to pay $300,000 each in fines. Tal Alexander, 40, was ordered to pay $350,000.

Caproni said she will ask the Bureau of Prisons to consult with experts about whether they should be allowed to be held together, as she believes they are bad influences on one another.

The men were found guilty in March of 10 counts, including conspiracy to commit sex trafficking and sex trafficking by force, after a trial that included testimony from 11 women who described being lured, drugged and sexually assaulted over a period of years.

Six of the women were part of the indictment.

In a sentencing memo, prosecutors in New York's Southern District said more than 70 women came forward with allegations of abuse and accused the brothers of exploiting their wealth, influence and connections to target victims.

Victim statements from 11 women, some using court-assigned pseudonyms, were read at the hearing before the judge's decision. The women asked Caproni to impose a sentence that was appropriate for the profound impact the men had on their lives.

One victim, Maya Miller, described the trauma of her rape by Tal Alexander as having settled into her nervous system.

"I carry a quiet funeral inside me," Miller said.

Another victim, Olivia Lane, told the judge that she was "profoundly incapacitated" after having had a fraction of one drink while meeting Oren Alexander. She described being raped at least a dozen times while she was terrified and in pain.

"You are weak. You are inhumane," Lane said. "You never had power, and look at you now."

Two women described the men as having almost inhuman eyes during their assaults. Isa Brooks said, "Their eyes went black during the attack, like I was being mauled by animals." Lane said, "I remember looking at him and seeing a monster, black eyes."

The women also emphasized the Alexander brothers' lack of remorse or acknowledgment of their victims throughout the trial. Victim Katie Moore noted in her statement that after five weeks of trial and having been found guilty, the men "cannot even look us in the eye as we speak today."

"These men spent years treating women and girls like their humanity meant nothing," Moore said.

The brothers honed their methods together, attacking women in a way that was designed to humiliate and degrade them, prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said at the sentencing.

"When they were done, they bragged to each other and their friends. ... The defendants knew exactly what they were doing, and they did it anyway, and they did it over and over and over again," she said.

At trial, prosecutors said the brothers raped the women after having promised them parties and trips. One woman testified that she lost control of her body after she had a drink with Alon Alexander at a New York City club.

When she awoke, she testified, they were naked on a bed. She kept trying to get up, and he kept pushing her back down, she said.

When she told him that she didn't want to have sex with him, she testified, he responded, "'You already did.'"

In a sentencing submission, attorneys for the brothers acknowledged that they sometimes behaved insensitively toward women but categorically denied that any of them had raped or sexually assaulted anyone.

At trial, the attorneys described the sex as consensual and said the women were motivated in part by financial gain.

"All the stories were rehearsed," Tal Alexander's attorney, Deanna Paul, said in her closing argument. "They're looking for money."

Paul urged the judge to consider giving her client the mandatory minimum of 15 years in prison, saying the verdict has not changed her view of the evidence. She said 15 years is already an extraordinary punishment, so "what would another 20 or 30 years accomplish?"

Attorneys for the two other brothers similarly asked Caproni to give the men 15 years. Marc Agnifilo, who represents Oren Alexander, told her the men all stopped their "sexually aggressive" behavior after they met their wives.

"All three defendants stopped, and that matters," Agnifilo said.

Each of the brothers was given an opportunity to address the court directly before he was issued his sentence.

Oren Alexander was the first to ask Caproni for a lighter sentence. He once again denied the assaults in his comments before he assaulted her that he has built a new life and family.

"My son needs me, and I need to be there for him, and I ask your honor to impose the minimum sentence," he said.

Tal Alexander, who was next to speak, expressed regret over his past actions. "The person who stands in court is not the same man as before," he said, asking Caproni to consider the entirety of his life in the decision.

"I wish I showed more maturity," he said. "I cannot undo moments when I was immature and careless with other people's feelings. I understand the jury found me guilty, and I know words cannot change that."

The last brother to speak, Alon, insisted that he was innocent and that he had never raped any women. He invoked his two young daughters in asking for the mercy of the court.

"I am afraid of being Daddy in the photograph," he said.

Caproni appeared unmoved by their statements, emphasizing that the rapes were not a result of "party culture or hookup culture" as they described. She said it was not enough to rape the women — the brothers sought to humiliate them, she asserted.

"That marriage would transform them from sexual predators to normal gentlemen, I disagree," Caproni said. "Rape is about power. ... Having a girlfriend or a wife doesn't mean you are not going to rape or humiliate women."

articles.title: Egypt orders closure of leading independent news site Mada Masr
articles.summary: Editor Lina Attalah was freed once a $53,400 fine was paid, only to learn of a one-year sentence passed in her absence.
articles.body:
An Egyptian court has ordered the closure of Mada Masr, one of the country’s last prominent independent news outlets, and fined its editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, three million Egyptian pounds ($53,400) for running a website without a licence.

The New Cairo Misdemeanour Court also ordered the confiscation of the outlet’s equipment and devices. Attalah was taken into custody after Tuesday’s ruling. She was released several hours later, after Mada Masr paid the fine in full.

During the release procedures, Attalah learned that she had been sentenced in absentia in 2024 to one year in prison, on charges of publishing false news and running an unlicensed website. Mada Masr said Attalah’s lawyers have challenged that ruling, and a retrial hearing is scheduled for November 11.

In an editorial published hours after the verdict, Mada Masr said it had entered court “with a measure of faith in the law and the justice system”. It added: “But what we found in court left none of that faith intact.”

The outlet said the court refused its lawyers’ requests to review the case file, submit additional evidence and call witnesses. According to Mada Masr, the judge then appointed “an unknown party” to act as Attalah’s defence lawyer, even though eight of her own lawyers were in court and she herself objected. The editorial said the judge wrote that lawyer’s requests himself “before issuing a verdict carrying the maximum penalty, with no review and no defence”.

Hossam Bahgat, head of the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, attended the hearing. According to Mada Masr, he said the court went ahead with the appointment despite Attalah’s own objection to being represented by a court-appointed lawyer. Mada Masr’s lawyer, Hassan al-Azhari, told the Egyptian outlet Zawia3 that the court rejected the defence’s requests and then appointed a lawyer, a step Attalah and her team objected to.

Tuesday’s ruling is based on Article 105 of Egypt’s 2018 media law, which sets fines of one to three million Egyptian pounds ($17,800–$53,400), plus closure and confiscation, for operating an unlicensed website.

Mada Masr says it applied for a licence from the Supreme Council for Media Regulation in 2018 and again in 2020, without a reply. It says it learned of a rejection only when prosecutors raised it during a previous case in 2022. In 2023, an administrative court upheld the council’s refusal, citing the absence of proof that the outlet’s trademark was registered, although Mada Masr’s lawyer said he had submitted a trademark registration certificate. A new application has been pending since June 2023.

There was no immediate official comment on the verdict.

The head of the Journalists’ Syndicate, Khaled el-Balshy, said the union would take legal action to appeal the ruling.

Mada Masr was founded in 2013 and has been blocked inside Egypt since 2017. It says it has faced six cases in six years, and rights groups say this is the first to reach trial.

“We tried to defend the law,” the outlet wrote, “just as we tried to defend ourselves.”

Amnesty International’s senior director for regional impact, Yasmine Ahmed, said in a statement, “Today’s decision represents a crushing blow to press freedom in Egypt and marks a dark day for independent journalism in the country.”

“This draconian ruling is the culmination of years of relentless harassment and unjust proceedings designed to shut down one of the country’s last remaining independent media voices,” Ahmed added.

The verdict came on the same day that Egypt’s Supreme State Security Prosecution, which investigates national security cases, renewed the detention of six journalists from the fact-checking platform Matsadaash for another 15 days.

articles.title: Alexander brothers each sentenced to 30 years in prison for sex trafficking case
articles.summary: The trio - two of whom were high-profile US real estate moguls - were found guilty using their social status to lure women to parties and then raping them.
articles.body:
Three brothers - two of them wealthy real-estate moguls - were sentenced to 30 years each in prison for drugging and raping dozens of women over decades.

Tal Alexander, 40, and twins Oren and Alon Alexander, 39, were found guilty in March of using their wealth and social status to lure women to parties and luxury homes, where they sexually assaulted them.

"Your conduct was monstrous," said Judge Valerie Caproni before sentencing them. "Your crimes wreaked havoc on their lives."

On Tuesday morning, the court in New York heard from 12 victims, including one who did not testify during the trial.

One by one, they spoke of the psychological trauma they endured after the Alexander brothers raped them, and their desire for the shame they had felt to instead fall on the defendants.

Many asked the judge to impose the maximum sentence of life in prison for each brother.

Maya Miller told the court that after Tal Alexander raped her in 2014, she lost all sense of safety. "I carry a quiet funeral within me for the person I might've become if this never happened to me," she said.

Another victim, using the pseudoym Isa Brooks, said after being raped by Tal and Alon Alexander when she was 16, she lost the ability to trust herself.

"I had no idea the danger I was in till it was too late," she said.

Another woman said when she planned to come forward about being raped, Tal Alexander threatened her, saying he knew where her sister worked.

Prosecutor Elizabeth Espinosa said the brothers deserved the maximum punishment for their crimes, saying facts "paint a truly devastating picture".

"For years, they honed their methods of luring women with the promise of luxury," she said, adding that they were "completely unmoved by the path of suffering they left behind them."

During the women's speeches, the three Alexander brothers showed little emotion. They stared ahead or conferred with their lawyers, who said they advised their clients not to look at the victims so it couldn't be misconstrued.

Attorneys for the brothers pushed for sentences of 15 years, arguing that they had become devoted fathers whose families would suffer in their absence.

The three men all addressed the court, continuing to profess their innocence.

"We had a work-hard, play-hard mentality," Tal Alexander said, adding he saw how his behavior "hurt people's feelings".

But their statements did not assuage Caproni, who chastised them for refusing to admit their crimes.

"How can someone who never acknowledged the wrongs they did be rehabilitated?" she asked.

At the end of the hearing, she sentenced them each to 30 years in prison for certain crimes. She also sentenced each to 20 years in prison for additional crimes, but said the men would serve the sentences concurrently.

During the five-week trial, 11 women - several said they were minors at the time of the assaults - testified that the brothers gave them gifts and flew them places including Aspen and the Bahamas where they fed them drugs before raping them.

Prosecutors said the brothers' pattern of abusive behaviour began in high school, though the trial involved crimes starting in 2008.

They said the three slipped drugs into women's drinks, and "physically restrained and held down their victims during the rapes and sexual assaults and ignored screams and explicit requests to stop".

Lawyers for the brothers argued the sex was consensual and that they were womanisers, but not abusers.

Two of the brothers, Tal and Oren, became wealthy selling luxury properties in New York and Miami.

They worked for American real estate giant Douglas Elliman, with clients including Lindsay Lohan, Kim Kardashian and Kanye West. In 2022, they founded their own New York-based firm called Official. Alon worked at the family's private security firm, Kent Security.

As they heard their sentences, the brothers stared straight ahead.

articles.title: US says it killed five people in strike on alleged drug boat
articles.summary: Latest strike brings death toll of campaign decried as extrajudicial killings to 243 people since September 2025.
articles.body:
The United States military has said that it has killed five people in a strike on an alleged drug trafficking boat in the eastern Pacific, continuing a campaign condemned by legal scholars and rights groups as extrajudicial killings .

US Southern Command (SOUTHCOM), which oversees military operations in Latin America and the Caribbean, said on Tuesday that five people were killed in the strike.

“On October 27, under the direction of SOUTHCOM, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Eastern Pacific,” it said in a social media post. “Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking. The operation killed five narco-terrorists.”

The administration of President Donald Trump has previously killed at least 238 people in 68 reported strikes in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific since the campaign first began in September 2025, according to a tracker from the Washington Office on Latin America (WOLA), a US-based research group that promotes human rights and democracy.

Tuesday’s strike appears to bring the reported total to 243 people. SOUTHCOM has often accompanied its announcements with videos that purportedly show vessels being struck.

The government has rarely shared details to substantiate its claims that those targeted are involved in drug trafficking, and relatives of some of those killed have said that they were fishermen or workers who were not involved in the drug trade.

The Trump administration has designated numerous criminal groups in Latin America as foreign “terrorist” organisations. Legal experts reject that framing and say that drug trafficking is a criminal activity against which military strikes are not permitted.

“This is the 6th lethal boat strike in the past 4 months,” Adam Isacson, an analyst at WOLA who has tracked the strikes, said in a social media post in response to SOUTHCOM’s announcement on Tuesday.

“The pace is slower than before, but the administration and its commanders persist in grinding out illegal killings every few weeks, with no discernible impact on the drug trade. A bleak pre-midterms message.”

articles.title: Dream postponed: Hebron groom caught in Israeli military lockdown
articles.summary: Israel’s military operation in West Bank’s Hebron has disrupted Palestinian life, including a postponed wedding.
articles.body:
Hebron, occupied West Bank – Haidar Yahya Tamimi had finished preparing his home, bought new furniture, chosen his wedding suit, and sent invitations to around 1,000 people. After four months of preparations, the 27-year-old was due to marry his fiancee, Ruba, on Friday.

Instead, he has been forced to leave his home in the al-Jalada neighbourhood, and the wedding has been postponed indefinitely.

Haidar is among thousands of Palestinians displaced by an Israeli military operation in Hebron that began after two Palestinian gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers at a checkpoint at the western entrance of the West Bank city on October 23. Both gunmen were killed by Israeli forces.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered an immediate lockdown in Hebron, and Israeli bulldozers destroyed buildings in the vicinity of the area where the attack took place, as well as going house to house in the neighbourhoods of al-Jalada and Ein Deir Baha, where the attackers lived.

By Monday, more than 3,100 Palestinians had been forcibly displaced, according to Hebron’s municipality.

Haidar has worked as a radiology technician at the Palestine Red Crescent Society Hospital in Hebron for about a year. He had been preparing to celebrate his wedding on Friday, with a feast scheduled for Thursday evening.

He and his fiancee had chosen the furniture for their new home together, as well as his wedding suit, a photograph of which he showed Al Jazeera.

But on the evening of October 23, as Hebron was declared a closed military zone after the attack, Haidar and his family were ordered to leave their homes along with other residents of al-Jalada and Ein Deir Baha. They departed in the middle of the night, taking only what they could carry.

Everything the couple had prepared for the wedding was inside the house, out of their reach. Haidar says they don’t know when they’ll be able to go back.

The groom was able to get to a spot nearby where he could see the house, but wasn’t able to get any closer due to the presence of the Israeli military.

“I looked at the house and saw that my dream was supposed to happen here, but it has been postponed indefinitely,” Haidar said.

He saw Israeli soldiers around the house, and says that relatives showed him security-camera footage of the soldiers entering his home. The current condition of the house is unknown.

As for the wedding, the couple have yet to set another date. First they need to know when they can return home.

Locals estimate that more than 100 businesses have been affected by the Israeli lockdown.

Consider the al-Jalada offices of Rukn al-Asala, a travel agent specialising in Muslim pilgrimage services. Agency manager Kamal al-Sharif, 35, has been unable to reach the office where he has worked with his father for 16 years.

The agency was organising an Umrah religious pilgrimage to Saudi Arabia for 15 people, set to depart on Wednesday. With the prospective travellers’ passports still in the office, and locals uncertain when the lockdown will end, that trip is likely to be postponed or cancelled.

Among the documents also inside the office are seven passports that Kamal says arrived from the Chinese embassy on October 22, the day before the lockdown. They belong to traders who had planned to travel to China on October 26.

The traders have their visas, but not their passports, and have been unable to travel, Kamal said.

One of the traders, a man in his 30s who did not wish to be named for security reasons, said he had been preparing to attend an exhibition in China where he could source equipment for his family business.

His flight and hotel bookings have now been cancelled – and the trader is stuck, not knowing when he’ll be able to get the products his business needs.

articles.title: In 2019, New Jersey completed the removal of the old Columbia Dam and reopened about 14 km of river; a 2026 study found juvenile eels, sea lampreys and American shad upstream after years of monitoring
articles.summary: Many dams today no longer serve their original purpose, and yet they continue to require costly maintenance.
articles.body: Many dams today no longer serve their original purpose, and yet they continue to require costly maintenance. For years, dams have hindered the natural course of rivers, preventing fish and other aquatic life from moving freely and causing damage not only to river ecosystems but also to the environment and overall water quality. One such dam that stood in the way of a New Jersey river was the Columbia Dam. The dam was finally removed in 2019, giving migratory fish the opportunity to swim upstream again. Now, a scientific study published in 2026 has found encouraging signs of recovery, including juvenile American eels, sea lampreys and adult American shad in areas above the former dam.The findings come from a long-term study published in Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution on April 13, 2026. Researchers monitored the Paulins Kill River in New Jersey over nine years, examining conditions before, during and after the dam's removal to understand whether the restoration was actually helping the river and its aquatic life recover.Why was the Columbia Dam removed?Built in the early 1900s by the Paulins Kill Consolidated Ice and Power Company, the dam created a pond that could supply water for the ice industry and generate energy for nearby communities, including Columbia in New Jersey and Stroudsburg in Pennsylvania. Over time, however, the structure became an obstacle for migratory fish that need to travel upstream to their breeding grounds to reproduce.Dams are well known to alter the natural flow of a river, affect water temperature and oxygen levels, interfere with sediment movement and prevent aquatic species from reaching suitable habitats. For fish that migrate between freshwater rivers and the sea, these barriers can be particularly challenging because reaching upstream areas may be essential for reproduction or access to suitable feeding grounds. As a result, the Columbia Dam was considered a priority for removal because of its location near the Paulins Kill's confluence with the Delaware River, a historically important route for migratory fish.The upstream flow of the lost fishThe health of fish populations within a river system, particularly migratory species, is a common indicator of river health. After the dam's removal in 2019, the 2026 study documented encouraging signs among several migratory species that had previously faced a barrier at the dam.Researchers recorded higher densities of juvenile American eels upstream of the former dam site, along with adult sea lampreys and their larvae. These findings suggest that migratory fish are once again accessing parts of the river that were previously difficult to reach.American eels have a particularly interesting journey, as they hatch in the Atlantic Ocean before their young travel towards freshwater rivers and streams, where they can spend years growing. The presence of juvenile eels upstream is therefore an encouraging sign that they can now reach habitats that were previously difficult to access because of the dam.Along with eels, sea lampreys also migrate through river systems, and their reproduction involves building nests in riverbeds where they lay their eggs. The study's findings of adults, larvae and nests upstream suggest that the restored river reach is being used for more than simply passage through the area.American shad, meanwhile, are migratory fish that travel from the ocean into freshwater rivers to reproduce. The presence of adult shad upstream adds to the evidence that removing the dam has helped reconnect habitats that were previously difficult for migratory fish to reach.Did removing the dam improve water quality?Fish returning to a river is one thing, but does removing an old dam also make the water healthier? To find out, scientists looked beyond the fish and studied how the river itself was changing after the Columbia Dam came down in 2019.The scientists also monitored water temperature, dissolved oxygen, turbidity and aquatic invertebrates at different points along the river. This allowed them to examine whether removing the dam had changed the physical conditions of the water, as well as the organisms living in it.The changes were small but measurable. Relative water temperature fell by around 0.29 degrees Celsius, while dissolved oxygen rose by 0.14 milligrams per litre. Dissolved oxygen is particularly important because fish and other aquatic organisms need it to survive, while water temperature can influence the species that are able to thrive in a river.However, these signs do not mean that the river has returned completely to its original state. Things can be destroyed in seconds but take years to rebuild. These results, though, offer encouraging signs of how the river has responded to being allowed to flow more freely.What the river's recovery tells us about dam removalAs said, removing a dam does not instantly restore a river to the way it was before, but it certainly gives a struggling ecosystem a chance to come back to life. When a barrier is taken away, migratory fish can reach stretches of water that were previously inaccessible, while the river's natural flow and the habitats around it can begin to change. The Columbia Dam's removal shows how even a single intervention can begin to reconnect an ecosystem that had been cut off for decades. The return of migratory fish and the changes observed in water conditions are encouraging signs, even if the river's complete recovery will take much longer. Sometimes, allowing nature to follow its own course is the first step towards restoring what years of human intervention had disrupted.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A 219-acre Florida cattle ranch facing development pressure was approved for a $20.15 million conservation easement in September 2026, allowing agriculture to continue while permanently restricting development
articles.summary: “The city kept expanding, and the village slowly kept letting go of its identity.
articles.body: “The city kept expanding, and the village slowly kept letting go of its identity. The village's name would just become the name of a neighbourhood or locality.” This thought, inspired by Vinod Kumar Shukla's Deewar Mein Ek Khirki Rehti Thi (A Window lived in the wall), captures what happens when urban expansion gradually swallows rural landscapes, turning once-independent villages into neighbourhoods surrounded by roads, houses and commercial developments. In Florida, however, a conservation agreement approved in September 2026 has given a 219-acre cattle ranch a chance to remain agricultural land instead of eventually giving way to development.According to a September 29 press release issued by the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS), the Leonard Property in Martin County has been protected from development through a rural land’s protection easement worth $20.15 million. The announcement was part of a wider initiative that secured protection for more than 4,500 acres of working agricultural land across Florida, allowing farms and ranches to continue their operations while placing permanent restrictions on future development.Why was the Florida cattle ranch facing development pressure?The Leonard Property covers approximately 219 acres in Martin County, Florida; its significant location has exposed it to development pressure. As land around is getting more and more inhabited by the growing communities, it has become an increasingly attractive for residential and other construction and expansion projects. The remaining agricultural properties are facing competing demands between remaining in farming and being put to alternative uses.According to the FDACS, the ranch consists of improved pastures, pine flatwoods, freshwater marshes and cypress systems, making it a landscape that combines working agricultural land with natural habitats. The property is also located within the Florida Wildlife Corridor, an ecosystem network of natural areas intended to help maintain connections between wildlife habitats across the state.Protecting the ranch therefore becomes even more important: it helps maintain land that supports agricultural activity while also preserving a landscape containing wetlands and other natural features that could be affected by future development.How does a conservation easement work?A conservation easement is a legal arrangement through which a landowner agrees to restrict certain uses of a property, usually to prevent development or protect its agricultural, ecological or historical value. In this case, the rural lands protection easement permanently restricts development while allowing the ranch to continue operating as agricultural land.Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program works so that, instead of purchasing the entire property, the developers only purchase development rights from landowners. This means that land can remain under private ownership, with its owners continuing agricultural operations even though they can no longer freely develop it in ways prohibited by the easement.Florida Commissioner of Agriculture Wilton Simpson explained the reasoning behind the programme in the official announcement, saying, “By permanently protecting working agricultural lands while keeping them in private ownership, we’re protecting Florida’s food supply and our rural way of life without taking the land off the tax rolls or creating new costs for the state.”The approach offers an alternative to buying farmland outright and converting it into state-owned conservation land. It also allows farmers and ranchers to continue their livelihoods while providing long-term protection against development that could otherwise change the character of rural areas.Who is paying to protect the ranch?The $20.15 million easement for the Leonard Property was approved as part of Florida's Rural and Family Lands Protection Program, with Martin County contributing $10.075 million towards the arrangement, according to the September 29 press release.The programme was established in 2001 to help preserve working agricultural lands as Florida's population growth and development put increasing pressure on rural properties. Rather than requiring farmers to stop agricultural activity, it aims to protect the land while allowing the production of food, timber and other resources to continue.The Leonard Property was one of seven agricultural properties included in the September 2026 announcement, which covered more than 4,500 acres of working agricultural land across Florida. The other properties included cattle ranches, a dairy operation, a sod and hay farm, and a timber operation, highlighting how the programme supports different types of agricultural businesses.Why protecting farmland matters beyond agricultureWhen a pasture or natural land turns into a concrete jungle, there’s little chance that grasses will grow there again or cattle will return to graze. These open fields not only give people space to breathe but also connect different habitats and allow animals to move around freely. Once buildings and roads take over, bringing the land back to what it once was becomes much harder.Central Park in New York City is one example of how people living in crowded cities still seek out green spaces to relax, walk or simply get away from the daily rush. This is why protecting farmland matters beyond agriculture, as losing these open spaces can affect both wildlife and the people who live around them.The Leonard Property's location within the Florida Wildlife Corridor makes its protection particularly important, as the surrounding landscape helps connect habitats and allows wildlife to move between natural areas. Its pastures, pine flatwoods and wetlands support both cattle ranching and the local environment.The agreement does not mean that development around the ranch will stop, nor does it turn the property into a public park. It simply means the land can continue to be used for agriculture without being opened up for development, even as the surrounding communities grow.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Finglas: Daniel Simion Toader charged with woman's murder
articles.summary: The victim, who was in her 40s, was found dead at a block of flats in Finglas on Monday morning.
articles.body:
A man has appeared in court charged with the murder of a woman who was found dead at a block of flats in the Republic of Ireland.

The woman has been named locally as Loredana Morosanu, who was in her 40s.

Her body was found at her home at Melville Terrace in Finglas, County Dublin when gardaí responded to an incident at the property at about 04.30 local time on Monday.

The court heard the accused, 47-year-old Daniel Simion Toader, who is Romanian, did not reply when gardaí (Irish police) charged him with murder.

The victim was originally from Romania but had lived in Ireland for several years.

The accused, also of Melville Terrace, appeared before Dublin District Court on Tuesday evening, dressed in a blue sweater, grey tracksuit bottoms and black shoes, according to Irish national broadcaster RTÉ.

He spoke only to a court-appointed interpreter and had no legal representation in court due to an ongoing legal aid pay dispute by Irish criminal defence lawyers.

A senior detective told the court that the suspect was arrested and charged with murder at Finglas Garda Station earlier on Tuesday evening.

He was remanded in custody until 3 November.

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after election loss, US says will grant visa
articles.summary: News comes one day after Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to hand over his passports in money-laundering probe.
articles.body:
A senior US State Department official said the Trump administration will issue visas to Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his family, allowing them to enter the US after news outlets reported that Bolsonaro fled Brazil after losing the country’s presidential election .

The news came on Tuesday, one day after Brazil’s Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro to turn over his passports as part of a probe into alleged money laundering. Bolsonaro has denied any wrongdoing and said on Monday that he had “never thought about leaving the country” and would stay to lead the opposition.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva , who has previously accused members of the Bolsonaro family of courting US interference in Brazilian affairs for their political benefit , called the right-wing senator’s actions shameful and said he should have stayed in the country to prove his innocence.

“A person who sneaks out of their country must have something to hide,” Lula said in the capital, Brasilia, during his 81st birthday celebration, adding that Brazil is the Bolsonaro family’s “second country” while the US is their first.

“The act of leaving Brazil is shameful.”

Bolsonaro, the son of former right-wing president Jair Bolsonaro, initially refused to acknowledge the election results and said he would seek their annulment. His party released a statement on Monday saying it accepted the results of the election, which the conservative candidate lost by more than 4.4 million votes.

US President Donald Trump reacted by casting doubt on the election result, telling reporters it “looked like another rigged election”.

No evidence has emerged that the vote was marred by malfeasance. While critics seized on a last-minute decision to extend polling hours, Lula’s eventual victory was commanding, and the extension was unlikely to change the outcome.

Democratic Representative Joaquin Castro said that Trump should tell the US Congress whether his administration played a role in Bolsonaro’s exit from Brazil.

“Losing an election is not grounds for asylum. Yet the Trump Administration is giving Flavio Bolsonaro safe haven in the United States. In Brazil, he is under investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering and currency evasion, and was ordered to surrender his passports,” Castro said in a social media post.

“The Trump Administration owes Congress answers on its role helping Bolsonaro flee Brazil in contravention of Brazilian law.”

Bolsonaro’s younger brother, Eduardo, who lives in the US and was convicted in absentia in June for illegally lobbying the Trump administration, said during a podcast interview earlier this month that Flavio should leave Brazil if he were to lose the race.

“If my brother does not win, I’m in favour that he would leave the country,” he told podcaster Steven Crowder.

articles.title: Nearly 200 unwanted concrete pipes and culverts were lowered into the Atlantic off Jacksonville in 2026; instead of being dumped on land, the pieces now form a new fish habitat roughly 90 feet below the water
articles.summary: Reefs were under threat in the ocean, so humans found a new solution by dumping construction waste onto the ocean floor.
articles.body: Reefs were under threat in the ocean, so humans found a new solution by dumping construction waste onto the ocean floor. Jokes aside, nearly 200 concrete pipes, culverts, and other structures that were no longer needed for construction projects have found a new purpose beneath the Atlantic Ocean off Florida’s coast. Rather than being discarded on land, these unwanted concrete structures have been lowered to the ocean floor, where they are expected to gradually become part of an underwater habitat for fish and other marine organisms.The artificial reef was installed at Harm’s Ledge, about 28 miles off the Mayport jetties near Jacksonville, Florida, at a depth of roughly 90 feet. The project was led by the Jacksonville Offshore Sport Fishing club, which worked with conservation groups, government agencies and private companies to turn surplus construction materials into a habitat that could support marine life while giving discarded concrete a practical second use.How discarded concrete is being turned into an underwater habitatThe concrete structures were loaded onto a barge using a forklift and transported to the offshore site, where they were carefully lowered to the seabed. The project was developed with support from Think It, Sink It, Reef It, an organisation involved in artificial reef initiatives that aim to create marine habitats using suitable recycled materials.The idea behind the installation is relatively simple, as much of the ocean floor off Northeast Florida consists of sand, which provides fewer hard surfaces for certain marine organisms to attach themselves to and fewer natural hiding places for fishes. By introducing these concrete structures with different shapes, openings and surfaces, the project creates spaces that marine life can gradually occupy and make home to.The openings in pipes and culverts can provide fish with places to shelter from predators, while the outer surfaces may attract algae, barnacles, corals and other organisms over time. As these organisms establish themselves, they can become part of a wider food web, potentially attracting smaller fish and other marine organisms that may eventually draw larger predatory species to the area. Creating a whole ecosystem around them.Why artificial reefs matter for marine lifeArtificial reefs, once a waste, are working wonders for Florida marine life and can provide shelter, feeding opportunities and potential spawning areas for fish and other marine organisms, particularly in locations where natural hard-bottom habitats are limited. Their surfaces offer attachment points for organisms that cannot easily establish themselves on loose sand, while the gaps and openings between structures create spaces where different species can live and feed.However, an artificial reef does not become a thriving marine ecosystem immediately after it reaches the seabed, and its long-term ecological value also depends on several factors, including water conditions, the composition of the materials and the species that eventually colonise the site. The presence of concrete alone does not guarantee an increase in fish populations, but appropriately designed and placed structures can provide useful habitat in suitable locations.For Jacksonville, the installation also represents a renewed effort to develop offshore reef habitats, with local reporting describing it as the city's first major artificial reef installation of this kind in several years. If marine organisms establish themselves successfully, the site could become another location where the region's underwater biodiversity can develop.A community effort to give construction materials a second lifeThe project began taking shape in early 2025, when the Jacksonville Offshore Sport Fishing Club and its partners explored the possibility of using donated concrete to create an offshore reef. The initiative subsequently involved grant applications, coordination with government agencies and contributions from private companies that supplied materials or helped with the work required to transport and sink the structures.The effort received support from organisations including the Jacksonville Waterways Commission, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission and the US Fish and Wildlife Service, alongside other partners. Bringing together fishing enthusiasts, conservation groups and businesses allowed materials that might otherwise have been discarded to be put to a new use, provided they were suitable for placement in the marine environment.Apart from its potential ecological benefits, the reef could eventually offer additional opportunities for recreational fishing and diving, although these activities will depend on how the site develops and the conditions surrounding it. Organisers also hope that the installation will contribute to a longer-term programme of offshore reef development in Northeast Florida.Jacksonville has a history of building artificial reefsThe latest installation builds on earlier reef-building efforts in the region, including a project carried out in 2000 and 2001, when volunteers and students from Mandarin High School helped create 500 dome-shaped concrete structures known as Reef Balls. These structures were placed offshore to establish the Charles H. Kirbo Memorial Reef between Jacksonville and St. Augustine.The new project follows a similar principle but uses surplus construction materials, including pipes and culverts, to create additional hard surfaces and sheltered spaces on the ocean floor. It also illustrates how materials that have outlived their original purpose can sometimes be repurposed for environmental projects rather than simply being sent for disposal.For now, the concrete structures mark the beginning of a gradual ecological process rather than a completed underwater ecosystem. As marine organisms begin to settle on the surfaces and fish explore the newly created spaces, researchers and project partners will have to observe how the site develops to understand the reef's actual contribution to the surrounding marine environment. For we know “one person's trash is another person's treasure.” And that’s how the construction worker became waste found a new calling, trading its life on land for a second chance at becoming a home for marine life.You use AI every day.
